content: Older adults diagnosed with diabetes should adhere to an optimal nutritional plan that includes adequate protein intake to support their overall health and metabolic needs. Engagement in regular physical activity is strongly recommended, encompassing aerobic exercises, weight-bearing activities, and balance training. These forms of exercise are crucial for maintaining physical functionality and preventing mobility-related complications. For older adults with type 2 diabetes who are also living with obesity, achieving a modest weight loss target, such as 5–7% of their body weight, should be considered. This level of weight reduction has been associated with significant improvements in quality of life and reductions in cardiometabolic risk factors. Lifestyle management strategies, which include a combination of balanced nutrition and regular physical activity, are vital for older adults. These interventions play a key role in preventing frailty, enhancing muscle strength, and minimizing the risk of falls and functional decline. Structured programs that emphasize dietary modifications and physical activity have demonstrated measurable benefits. Collectively, these outcomes contribute to an enhanced quality of life for older adults with diabetes.
